question: Is 1024-entry oldest-entry eviction acceptable for Google Chat approval action-token bindings and manual follow-up suppressions under high-cardinality approval traffic?
rationale: Automation can verify the unbounded Maps and the bounded implementation, but the cap intentionally changes how long older pending approval state remains usable under load.

options.title: Accept the bounded registries
options.body: Merge after final exact-head checks if maintainers accept that pending Google Chat approval state older than the newest 1024 entries can be evicted before expiry.

options.title: Tune cap or eviction semantics
options.body: Ask for a higher limit, per-approval grouping, TTL-aware pruning, or instrumentation if pending approval usability must be preserved for larger workloads.

options.title: Pause this PR
options.body: Pause or close the PR if bounded memory is not worth changing high-cardinality approval-card lifetime semantics now.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded registries
recommendation.body: Merge after final exact-head checks if maintainers accept that pending Google Chat approval state older than the newest 1024 entries can be evicted before expiry.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the native Google Chat approval-card registry and are the strongest history owner for the affected lifetime behavior.
